note: After Banks's (1901) original description of the new species (in English), there placed in the genus Calotermes (Calotermes galapagoensis sp. nov.) and later transferred to Incisitermes; only the alate is described. The original gives only two total-length figures and no measurements of individual parts.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Yellowish brown; the mouthparts, antennae, legs and underside paler; wings nearly transparent, the subcosta and its branches brown, the costal area slightly tinged with dark. Head rather wide, the compound eyes before the midpoint, ocelli present. Pronotum much wider than long, slightly narrower than the head, the posterior margin rounded, the middle of the dorsum with a pale line. Length of the abdomen about equal to the head and thorax together. Wings much longer than the body, rather broad, pointed at the apex; the subcosta branches only beyond the middle of the wing; the media lies between the subcosta and the submedia, its branches as usual and simple, only the proximal branches forked.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Measurements: body length including the wings 9.5 mm, body length 5 mm. Collecting: Wenman Island, December (month 12), several specimens. The original describes the alate only; at the beginning of the section on the Termitidae the author states that both termites collected on the island differ from the known species and that, when the Central American fauna is better known, these two may also be found to occur in that region.
